messaging.transportSplit: Kafka carries domain events only. SQS carries task jobs only. Synchronous request/response stays HTTP. A workload never appears on both transports.

envelope.type: Event name and Kafka topic in one field. After contracts 2.0.0 there is no separate topic or eventType field.
envelope.version: Per-event integer, starts at 1. Consumers reject unknown versions or route them to the DLQ.
envelope.idempotencyKey: Producer-owned stable key. Consumers persist it in processed_events in the same transaction as the side effect.
envelope.keying: Kafka message key is the aggregate id: orderId, cartId, productId, categoryId, blogId, userId, or sessionId.

delivery.commit: Manual commit only after the side effect and the processed_events insert commit together.
delivery.dlq: Every source topic has a <topic>.dlq twin. Malformed JSON and invalid known payloads go directly to the DLQ. Unknown event types are ignored and committed with a metric.
delivery.consumerGroups: One consumer group per service, not per service+topic. Nest postfixId is set to an empty string so groups do not gain a -server suffix.
delivery.idempotency: Postgres processed_events table or Mongo processed_events collection with a unique (consumer, event_id) index.

implementation.library: @nestjs/microservices Kafka transport for consumers plus a kafkajs producer for the outbox relay. Domain code never imports kafkajs directly.
implementation.outbox: All five producers are on the shared @ecom/messaging 0.2.0 package, with two stores behind one port. Postgres (auth, cart, catalog, order): <schema>.outbox written in the same transaction as the domain change, claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED under a session advisory lock per schema, published sequentially keyed by aggregate id, marked published, retried with a locked_until backoff, parked at failed after five attempts. Mongo (cms): cms_outbox written in the same session transaction as the document write and the revision bump, claimed by repeated atomic findOneAndUpdate on status 'pending' with an expired lease, guarded by a lease document in cms_outbox_locks. Identifiers are quoted, so the reserved-word schema "order" is addressable. catalog's producer-side KafkaEventBus and cms's direct cms.events publish are deleted; cms media.tasks stays on the direct bus until cms-006 moves it to SQS.
implementation.consumer: @EventPattern handlers with @Payload and @Ctx KafkaContext on one strategy per service, over the shared @ecom/messaging 0.3.0 consumer surface: createKafkaConsumerStrategy (postfixId ''), KafkaEventHandler (parse, retry ladder, dead letter, counter, manual commit in that order), ProcessedEventsStore, KafkaDlqPublisher, KafkaLagSampler. A service contributes only its routes and its handler; the protocol lives in the package. @ecom/contracts envelope validation runs before the side effect, and a failed DLQ write throws KafkaConsumerStalledError instead of committing past a lost record.
implementation.topics: Auto-create is disabled. ecom-infra creates every topic and its .dlq twin with explicit partitions and retention.
implementation.noDirectPublish: Request handlers never publish directly. They write an outbox row; the relay publishes it.

topics.note: No Kafka consumer in v1. Storefront cache invalidation uses an HTTP webhook so the storefront never holds Kafka credentials.
Storefront sends an HTTP beacon to Next /api/track; analytics-svc validates it and publishes the event.

taskQueues.note: Created after a Kafka consumer maps an event to an email. Never a Kafka topic.
Catalog-svc does not upload media in v1. If it does later it enqueues the same queue.

nonKafka: SQS tasks: notify-send-email, import-process-row, media-resize-image. Tasks never go to Kafka.
Storefront page views: sendBeacon -> Next /api/track -> analytics-svc HTTP -> Kafka. The storefront holds no Kafka credentials.
Storefront CMS cache invalidation: CMS calls Next /api/revalidate over HTTP with a shared secret. No storefront Kafka consumer.
Admin app: API/HTTP only. No direct Kafka producer or consumer.
Search backfill and tests: internal batch HTTP endpoint. Kafka replay is not the backfill mechanism.
Cart conversion: order.created event. Phase 0 may use a temporary internal HTTP endpoint until the consumer lands.
Synchronous cross-service reads: internal REST (catalog snapshots, auth email lookup, order lookup).
No SNS, MSK, EventBridge, or per-consumer SQS fan-out in v1.

workflow: Claim: create TASKS/in-progress/<id>-<slug>.md, set the entry status to in-progress, owner, and started. Build against the chained skills (router order). Close: move the log to TASKS/done/, fill verification and follow_ups, flip status to done and finished, update STATUS.md and summary in the same commit. Todo entries carry log:null until claimed; in-progress and done entries must have an existing log file. Commits: one commit per file (larger edits split per edit); stage with diff eyes-on; subject + reason body; local-only until the human says push. Unpushed lists only verified local commits; the carrier commit joins on the next update. Validation: id == filename, status == folder, log exists for in-progress/done, STATUS counts == summary. Before any tracker commit, run scripts/validate-tasks.py and require exit 0. followUpAudit must classify every original follow-up; counts are derived from entries, never hand-set.
rules: Claim: set claimedBy={agent,since,task} + stages.<stage> to in-progress (24h lease; other instances must not steal without comment). Finish: flip stage to done + update SERVICES.md + STATUS.md in same commit. Stage vocab locked: todo|in-progress|done (maps to todo/in-progress/done cells). Path truth: localRoots below are where agents edit TODAY; future split repos named in 'repo'. Never invent paths — resolve via SKILL-EXPLORE. motive is immutable (ADR change only); inProgress/next are mutable. Transport truth: Kafka is domain events only, SQS is task jobs only; each repo messaging block and the top-level messaging catalog are authoritative.

sf_at lives at Path=/ for 15m, sf_rt at Path=/api/auth for 30d, both HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax and Secure in production. Reason: an ordinary page request must never carry the refresh token.

Logout is POST-only and succeeds even when auth-svc is down. Reason: SameSite=Lax still sends cookies on a top-level cross-site GET, so a GET link would let any page sign a shopper out.

tasks.title: storefront: CMS source wiring and revalidate webhook
key_decisions: Every CMS read is fetch(url, { next: { tags: [cmsTag], revalidate: 300 } }); the Next Data Cache is the cross-request layer. Reason: a shared cache, a purge handle and a staleness bound in one argument. Rejected: ioredis in the storefront (no purge handle, a Redis credential in a public app).

The cascade is cms-svc -> a bounded 32-entry in-process TTL entry -> DEMO_NAV_INPUT, and the root layout has no throwing path. Reason: a cms-svc restart must not blank every route. Rejected: no fallback at all; an unbounded map keyed by page; redirect on CMS failure.

POST /api/revalidate is secret-gated (constant-time over the SHA-256 of both sides, fails closed when the env var is unset) and rejects any tag outside lib/cms/tags.ts. Reason: unvalidated, one loop flushes the whole cache. Rejected: an open endpoint; a bearer JWT; revalidatePath('/').

revalidateTag(tag, 'max') once per tag, and the tag vocabulary is one module shared by readers and the webhook. Reason: string literals at both ends would let a typo silently disable invalidation forever. Rejected: per-call literals.

Local structural guards instead of @ecom/contracts response schemas. Reason: the pinned 1.7.0 tarball does not export them and the repin is sf-053's job; the resolvers already degrade every inner field. Rejected: a cross-repo version bump hidden inside a UI task.

ecom-messaging.note: Created by au-004/ca-008 and tracked through those two tasks, so its tasks array is empty and it adds no rows to summary.byRepo on purpose. 0.2.0 (pre-1.0, breaking allowed): OutboxStorePort<Ctx = Queryable>, PostgresOutboxStore (now quoting "schema"."table", which is what made order.outbox addressable), MongoOutboxStore (atomic per-document claim, lease-document relay lock), shared OutboxRelay, createOutboxModule + createMongoOutboxModule, and an always-registered OutboxInitializer that creates indexes even when the relay is off. ESM with a framework-free '.' entry and a './nest' factory; peer @ecom/contracts >=1.8.0 <2, with kafkajs and @nestjs/common optional. Distributed as a committed tarball pinned with file:, like ecom-contracts. 39 unit tests; needs no database and no broker. All five producers (auth, cart, catalog, order, cms) are repinned to 0.2.0 and share one package version. 0.3.0 (additive, 2026-11-01, srch-002/ca-009/cat-008): the consumer surface. KafkaEventHandler.run(ctx, topic, raw, handle) is the only place the protocol is written down, in the order side effect -> counter -> offset: JSON.parse failure -> DLQ invalid-json with rawValue and commit; handle() returns applied/duplicate/ignored/invalid; invalid -> DLQ before the counter and before the commit; a throw -> 1/2/4/8/16s ladder then DLQ transient-exhausted, committing only after the DLQ ack; an optional translateError makes service-specific terminal errors dead-letter immediately. run() never throws except KafkaConsumerStalledError when the DLQ write itself failed, which stops the loop on purpose. Also ProcessedEventsStore (claim = INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING under the caller's transaction), KafkaDlqPublisher (<topic>.dlq via the registry with a suffix fallback), KafkaLagSampler (fetchTopicOffsets minus fetchOffsets, -1 counted as never-committed), nine counters, and createKafkaConsumerStrategy (postfixId '', autoCommit false, string deserializer). Peer floor rose to @ecom/contracts >=1.9.0 <2 and @nestjs/microservices ^12.0.1 became an optional peer; cart-svc stays on contracts 1.8.0 deliberately and is the one known pin mismatch. Consumers on 0.3.0: cart-svc, catalog-svc, search-svc (vendored). Producers stay on 0.2.0 (auth, cms, order) — re-pinning a producer buys nothing until 1.0.0. 100 unit tests (9 files). 0.3.0 adds the consumer surface's own suite: kafka-event-handler (every step of the protocol, including DLQ-failure ordering), processed-events.store (claim/duplicate/rollback), dlq.publisher (registry names plus the fallback), lag.sampler (the -1 case and multi-partition), kafka-consumer.strategy (postfixId and autoCommit), consumer-metrics.

tasks.title: cms-svc: Mongo transaction + cms_outbox for cms.updated and blog.updated
key_decisions: Write content, the revision bump and cms_outbox in one Mongo session transaction; publish cms.updated on cms.updated, not cms.events. Reason: the current direct publish can diverge from content and the relay keys on event_type, so a cms.events row would be an unknown topic. Rejected: best-effort publish after save, or teaching the relay about transport aliases.

Add MongoOutboxStore behind the existing OutboxStorePort instead of a cms-local relay. Reason: one relay means one set of claim/lease/backoff semantics; a local copy duplicates exactly what the package exists to prevent. Rejected: a CMS-specific relay.

Generalise the port as OutboxStorePort<Ctx = Queryable> so Mongo can pass a session while the four Postgres call sites stay source-compatible. Reason: the seam's only type safety is the context type. Rejected: write(client: unknown).

Claim Mongo rows with repeated atomic findOneAndUpdate (one document per call, up to limit). Reason: that is the Mongo analogue of FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; find + updateMany can double-claim between the two round trips. Rejected: a single updateMany.

Guard the Mongo relay with a lease document (findOneAndUpdate with upsert) instead of insertOne as a mutex. Reason: Mongo has no advisory locks, and a crashed relay must not hold the lock forever. Rejected: an insert-based lock.

Invalidate the Redis cache after the commit, never inside the transaction. Reason: Redis cannot join a Mongo transaction; invalidating first lets a reader re-cache the pre-commit state. Rejected: invalidate-then-commit.

Pass the session into RevisionService.bumpVersion. Reason: a document and a revision that can disagree is the same defect as a document and an event that can disagree, and the payload carries the version. Rejected: bump after commit and stamp the reported version.
Keep media.tasks on the direct CMS bus. Reason: it is not an EventTopic, so the relay would park it; cms-006 moves it to SQS. Rejected: a fake topic in the registry.

Create the cms_outbox indexes from store.initialize() at boot, not from a hand-applied migration. Reason: one definition of the indexes for every environment, including when the relay is disabled in tests. Rejected: a JS migration outside the package.

tasks.title: search-svc + messaging: composite document identity, session-bounded retry ladder, trustworthy reindex
key_decisions: Identity is the composite primary key (document_type, id): migration 004 drops PRIMARY KEY (id) and the now-redundant search_documents_type_id_key, and the fresh-install DDL matches. Reason: the single-column PK outranked the ON CONFLICT (document_type, id) arbiter, so a cross-type id collision was a 23505 no retry can ever clear. Rejected: re-point the upsert at ON CONFLICT (id), which would let a category document overwrite a product one.

The consumer strategy sets sessionTimeout 45000 and heartbeatInterval 3000 explicitly. Reason: nothing set them before, so kafkajs's 30s default owned a production contract and evicted the member mid-ladder, killing both the DLQ write and the commit with UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID. Rejected: raise only the session timeout, which leaves the ladder unbounded for the next handler that adds a delay.

KafkaEventHandler takes retryBudgetMs and truncates retryDelaysMs at construction so the total sleep stays inside the session; search-svc passes 20000, giving 1000/2000/4000/8000 over 5 handler attempts. Reason: the budget belongs with whoever owns the ladder, and the truncated ladder also matches the maxReceiveCount 5 parity the SQS relay already claims. Rejected: cap the sleep at retry time per message, which cannot keep maxRetries and the ladder length honest.

A SQLSTATE 23505 from the index write is terminal: translateIndexError maps it to index-constraint-violation and the record dead-letters on attempt 1 with the offset committed. Reason: redelivery cannot repair a deterministic constraint breach, and walking the ladder over one is exactly what wedged the partition. Rejected: treat it like a transient DB failure and retry, which stalls the group for a record that will never succeed.

reindex.mjs reads exactly one complete page per document type and refuses a type whose response carries nextCursor; a type that fails to load is dropped from the payload instead of half-loaded. Reason: IndexerService.pruneMissing runs per type present in the payload, so a partial read deletes live documents - the first run pruned 6 and reported success while products were never read at all. Rejected: walk the products cursor, which is not exhaustive (page 2 repeats 78 of page 1's 100 rows), and rejected: fix catalog-svc in this wave, which is a different repo's contract.

Dev databases stop applying 002-seed-search.sql; the index is populated by events plus pnpm search:reindex, and the seed stays ecom_search_test-only. Reason: the seed hand-authors category ids that collide with catalog product fixture ids, orphaning rows in the shared dev index. Rejected: edit the seed, which is the e2e suite's fixture and whose count assertions the suite depends on.
acceptance: search_documents has PRIMARY KEY (document_type, id) and no search_documents_type_id_key, in migration 004, the fresh-install DDL and the live dev and test databases.

The same id can exist as a product and as a category at once, and an ON CONFLICT (document_type, id) upsert of the colliding id writes instead of raising; pruneMissing leaves the same-id row of another type alive.
The emitted Kafka consumer config carries sessionTimeout 45000 and heartbeatInterval 3000, and an explicit option overrides either.
With retryBudgetMs the ladder's total sleep stays within the budget and the attempt count follows the truncated ladder; without it the ladder is exactly 1/2/4/8/16s.
A 23505 from the repository dead-letters on the first attempt as index-constraint-violation and the offset still commits - no ladder walked.

Live boot drains without Exhausted retries or UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID, product.updated partition 2 advances past the old offset-61 wedge, and the index matches its sources (16 products, 9 categories, 3 blogs, zero orphans).
Docs state the composite identity and the bounded-ladder rule; search-svc README separates the development database from the e2e test database.
